# Phase Status Board

A single live table of numbered phases, each carrying a colour, a status, and — the part that does the
work — an explicit **"Remaining:"** line naming what is not done. It replaces the binary
done/not-done checklist with something that can express *code exists but has never met reality*.

[[farely]]'s `02-roadmap.md` runs fourteen phases with four states: 🟢 done · 🟡 in progress ·
⚪ not started · 🔴 blocked.

## Why the extra states earn their place

Two labels carry almost all the information:

- **"done (sim)"** — Phases 6b and 11 are marked green *with a qualifier*. The feature works in the
  browser simulator; it has not worked anywhere else. Without that suffix they would be
  indistinguishable from genuinely finished work.
- **"code-complete — remaining: validate on device"** — Phases 2, 3, 6, 7 and 12. This is the honest
  name for the most common state in a solo prototype and the one a checkbox cannot express at all.

Phase 5 — field testing on a real phone with real offers — sits at ⚪ **not started**.

## The board told the truth

This is the finding worth keeping. Farely's README overstates its test coverage and its privacy
posture, and four documents describe an OCR engine that is a stub — see [[documentation-drift]]. The
roadmap board is the one artifact in the repo that did **not** drift:

> "Only the web simulator, never the APK on a live shift."
> — interview, 2026-07-28

Which is exactly what a board reading *Phase 5 ⚪ not started* and five phases at *remaining: validate
on device* had been saying all along. A structured status table with a mandatory "remaining" field
resists optimism in a way that prose does not, because leaving the field blank is visibly a lie while
writing a confident sentence is not.

Contrast the same repo's index README:

> "**Phase 0 — Documentation.** No native code merged yet"
> — Farley/docs/ocr-overlay/README.md, 2026-07-02

Same repo, same directory, thirteen phases apart. The difference is that the board is the file the
author returned to; the index is prose written once.

## Where the pattern is weak

The board records *engineering* completion, not *value* completion. Every green phase in Farely is
green against a simulator, and no phase asks "did this earn money" — which is why
{{deadhead-adjusted-net-profit}}'s constants could stay unvalidated with the board still looking
healthy. A status board bounds the claim "the code exists"; it cannot bound "the code is right".
